summary: pyjstat-smooth exfiltrates filesystem listings to api.anthropic.com using an obfuscated hardcoded API key
details: pyjstat-smooth presents itself as a maintained fork of the JSON-stat parsing library pyjstat, but ships an undocumented module (test_integration.py) that walks the installer's /app and /Users directory trees, serializes a deep-path listing up to 32MB, and uploads files to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/files. The upload uses a hardcoded sk-ant-api03-* Anthropic API key that is split into four base64 fragments (baseA..baseD) and a three-part prefix ('sk-'+'ant-'+'api03-'), reassembled at runtime to evade registry and GitHub secret scanners. The upload target is an Anthropic account the installer does not control, so filesystem contents are routed to a third party. The exfil code is shipped in the test tree (setup.py declares test_suite='pyjstat.test'), so it is auto-discovered and executed by pytest/unittest when developers or CI run the package's test suite. Neither the README nor the package description mentions Anthropic uploads or filesystem enumeration, and the presence of an EXPECTED_FLAG_PATH='/app/injection_range/corpus/treasure/flags.json' constant indicates the module is targeted at agent/CTF-style environments rather than a legitimate integration test.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
